content.text:
The renderer is implemented and all 12 tests pass (the public smoke test plus 11 of mine under `tests/unit`). **What I built** - `src/markdown.js` exports `render(markdown)`. It is a thin wrapper around the vendored commonmark.js 0.31.2 parser and HTML renderer. The one piece of glue overrides raw HTML so it is escaped as text rather than passed through. - Raw HTML: inline HTML is escaped as text. Block HTML is escaped and wrapped in `

…

`. The spec doesn't say how block HTML should be wrapped, so this is my choice. - The CommonMark behaviour the spec describes (emphasis rules, lists, code fences, escaping, thematic breaks, soft breaks) comes from the reference library. **Retrieval protocol** - Searched GitHub (`gh-search`) and npm (`npm-search`). I did not run a Stack Overflow search. - Chose `commonmark` 0.31.2 (BSD-2-Clause) as the reference implementation the spec names. - Vendored it into `src/vendor/commonmark/`, along with its two dependencies at the versions it pins: `mdurl` 1.0.1 (MIT) and `entities` 3.0.1 (BSD-2-Clause). - Both dependencies are CommonJS. I put a `package.json` with `"type":"commonjs"` in each vendored directory and bridged `entities` through a small `createRequire` shim (`src/vendor/entities-shim.js`). Nothing is installed from npm at runtime. - Nothing was written from scratch; the only new code is the glue in `src/markdown.js`, the shim, and my tests. **Records** - `PROVENANCE.json` lists all three vendored packages with source, license, paths, and how each was adapted. - `src/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` gives the attribution for each. **Behaviour to be aware of** - The vendored library implements full CommonMark, which is a superset of the spec subset. Inputs outside the subset (setext headings, indented code blocks) follow CommonMark rather than being rejected. For example, `para\n---` renders as an `

`.
